title: mitigate-admission-skew-leading-to-small-request-suppression-under-mixed-length-loads
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported tail latency regressions for short, low-token requests during mixed-load periods where a few long-context generations overlap with many short queries. Root cause appears to be an admission scoring imbalance in the continuous-batching admission controller: long requests dominate admission weight and cause small requests to be deferred repeatedly, producing effective starvation for latency-sensitive flows across Hosted and Dedicated deployments.

Impact: High. Multiple production escalations in the last 72 hours from two enterprise customers on Dedicated pools and three Hosted tenants. Observed symptom set: p50 for short requests unaffected, but p95/p99 spikes by 3-8x during bursts. Visible increase in request queueing time and KV-cache churn. Some private deployments reported similar behavior after recent autoscaler tuning.

How to reproduce: 1) Start a mixed load generator with 10k short requests per minute (50-150 tokens) and 15 concurrent long requests (4k+ tokens) arriving periodically. 2) Observe admission decisions and queue wait times using the staging scheduler diagnostics. 3) Short requests get repeatedly preempted when long sequences enter the admission window; queue time builds up.

Hypothesis: The admission score formula multiplies backlog-weight by sequence-length penalty and a moving-average fairness factor. In pathological mixes, the product skews strongly in favor of long requests because the length penalty is unbounded and backlog-weighting increases with tenant concurrency.

Proposed fixes (incremental plan):
- Short term (hotfix, P0): Clip the length penalty multiplier and introduce a small-request priority boost in admission scoring for latency-classified routes. Implement a fast feature-flagged override so changes can be disabled quickly.
- Mid term: Add a tiny reserved admission slot (1-2 slots per GPU core) for latency-sensitive short requests to ensure forward progress during microbursts of long contexts.
- Long term: Replace multiplicative score with normalized additive scoring with explicit caps per-class and adaptive decay to avoid backlog amplification. Add a backpressure signal to ingress to shed or divert large-batch long-context requests to burst capacity.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.
comments: 2026-01-28 - Maya Chen: Filed after triage call with SRE and Customer Success. Attached initial flame graphs and scheduler traces. Customer incident IDs: INC-2026-1023, INC-2026-1041.

2026-01-29 - Luca Moretti: Confirmed reproducible in local cluster using 'mixbench' harness. Created prototype that clamps length-penalty to max=3. Observed 40-60% reduction in short-request p99 in synthetic tests.

2026-01-30 - Priya Nair (SRE): Runbook updated with temporary mitigation: enable admission-clip flag per-pool. Rolling enablement in eu-west-1 dedicated pools reduced customer p99 spikes within 1 hour.

2026-02-01 - Design review (offline): Agreed to preserve absolute throughput for long jobs while protecting latency-sensitive paths. Decided to add per-route metadata to classify latency sensitivity; PM will own opt-in list.

2026-02-03 - Code review feedback from Rafael Gomez: Request to add exhaustive unit tests around boundary conditions and to document overflow behaviors for the legacy scoring formula. Filing follow-up test ticket ENG-47671.

2026-02-04 - Canary: Deployed feature-flagged fix to hosted-canary region (hosted-canary-3). Observed short-request p95 improved from 280ms to 85ms under mixbench scenario. No regression in overall throughput. Monitoring alert thresholds lowered pending broader rollout.
2026-02-05 - Customer Success: Communicated remediation path to affected customers; provided ETA for full rollout and rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: Flagged change deploys behind feature flag and can be toggled without restart
Synthetic mixbench tests show short-request p95 reduced by >=50% vs pre-fix under representative load
No reduction in sustained throughput for long-context workloads beyond 5% in perf tests
Canary in hosted-canary and two dedicated pools for 48 hours without new escalations
Automated unit and integration tests cover adversarial admission sequences and boundary clipping
